title: The International System of Units (SI), 9th edition
source: Bureau International des Poids et Mesures, The International System of Units (SI), 9th edition 2019, version 4.01 (June 2026), chapter 5 "Writing unit symbols and names, and expressing the values of quantities", https://doi.org/10.59161/AUEZ1291, read 2026-10-08.

rules.text: A space separates the number from the unit symbol, also when the value is used as an adjective (a 10 kΩ resistor).
The degree Celsius is spaced like any unit: 20 °C, not 20°C or 20° C.
No space comes before the degree, minute and second of a plane angle: 30° 22′ 8″.
A space separates the number and the symbol %: 5 %.
Unit symbols are lower case unless named after a person, and are never abbreviations: s not sec, cm³ not cc, m/s not mps.
A unit symbol takes no plural and no full stop, except the full stop that ends a sentence.
A solidus is used at most once in a unit unless parentheses remove the ambiguity.
Unit symbols and unit names are not mixed in one expression.
A value is given in one unit: 10.234 m, not 10 m 23.4 cm.
What qualifies a quantity goes with the quantity, not the unit: a maximum voltage of 1000 V, not 1000 Vmax.
Long numbers may be grouped in threes by a space, never by a dot or a comma.
